newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close higher despite U.S. rate news.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close higher despite U.S. rate news.

text.p: * Main index ended 19.02 pnts up, 0.59 pct, to 3,223.14 pnts

The Philippine equities market closed higher on Wednesday as players ignored news of a boost in U.S. interest rates and instead positioned themselves ahead of a projected stock uptick after the Easter holidays, traders said.
"People started realising that maybe they should start buying stocks in anticipation of a recovery," said Caesar Tanquingcen, a trader at Connell Securities Inc.
Value turnover remained light at 2.064 billion pesos.
"We already expected the increase in U.S. rates and so the market did not react further," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, Diversified Securities Inc executive vice-president.

The main index registered mild gains for most of the session and a late buying surge in index heavyweights Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and Ayala Land Inc boosted the market's barometer further, traders said.
Gainers outnumbered losers 69 to 49 with 73 issues unchanged.
Traders said the listing of Equitable Corp on April 3 will enhance market liquidity. Investor positioning ahead of first quarter earnings reports may trigger an uptrend, they added.
